defects: Introduces an arbitrary uninterpreted function `natTrunc : Cardinal → ℕ` as a hypothesis parameter instead of referencing the actual `Cardinal.toNat` function, losing all connection to what toNat actually is/does

Hypothesis is structurally different: gold compares `n ≤ c` (the coerced natural number compared to the cardinal itself, in Cardinal's order) for all n, while produced compares `natTrunc c₁ ≥ n` (the already-truncated natural number compared to n, in ℕ's order) — this is not the same condition

Because of the above two changes, the produced statement becomes a trivial/tautological fact true for ANY function into ℕ (or any linearly ordered type) via antisymmetry, and no longer expresses the substantive mathematical content of the gold theorem about cardinal truncation
Drops universe polymorphism: gold allows c and d to live in different universes (Cardinal.{u}, Cardinal.{v}), produced does not
